questions.question: What precision target motivates the paper's simultaneous photon- and gluon-resummation framework for luminosity processes?

options.A: A 2% theory tag to match the experimental luminosity tag
options.B: A 0.67% theory tag so theory does not dominate a 2% experimental tag
options.C: A 0.3% experimental tag to match the expected QED correction
options.D: A 1.0% theory tag only for the Tevatron measurements

questions.rationale: The introduction assigns a 0.67% theoretical precision requirement given 2% experimental luminosity precision.
questions.evidence_quote: should be at the 0.67% level in order not to compromise

questions.question: What is the structural basis of the authors' QCD exponentiation, as distinguished from an approximate exponentiation prescription?

options.A: An exact rearrangement based on the N=1 exponent term, supplemented by residuals accounting for the rest of the series
options.B: An approximate soft-collinear factorization that retains only leading double logarithms
options.C: A truncation of the perturbative series at exact O(αs²), followed by a parton shower
options.D: A path-ordered exponential whose matrix elements are not evaluated

questions.rationale: They describe an exact rearrangement built from the N=1 exponent term and all-order residual functions.
questions.evidence_quote: an exact rearrangement of the QCD perturbative series based on the N = 1 term

questions.question: In the combined QED⊗QCD construction, how are the QED infrared functions incorporated into the QCD ones?

options.A: They replace the QCD functions because QED has no real-emission singularities
options.B: They are added term-by-term to the corresponding QCD functions to form QCED functions
options.C: They enter only the hard residuals, leaving the exponent purely QCD
options.D: They multiply the QCD functions by the electric charge squared after integration

questions.rationale: Equation (3) defines each QCED infrared function as the sum of its QCD and QED analogs.

questions.question: What physical distinction explains the compensation needed to isolate infrared-finite QCD residuals?

options.A: QCD has genuine non-Abelian virtual and real singularities that compensate between neighboring multiplicities, unlike QED
options.B: QED virtual singularities cancel only after PDFs are introduced, whereas QCD is finite per multiplicity
options.C: QCD collinear poles are absent, while QED soft poles remain at each order
options.D: Non-Abelian color averaging removes all gluon singularities before phase-space integration

questions.rationale: The text emphasizes the real/virtual compensation between n- and n+1-particle phase-space terms as distinguishing QCD from QED.
questions.evidence_quote: the essential compensation between the left over genuine non-Abelian IR virtual and real singularities

questions.question: What does the paper say about the relative onset of QCD- and QED-dominant corrections in its infrared algebra?

options.A: QED corrections dominate an order of magnitude earlier because Qf² exceeds CF
options.B: QCD-dominant corrections occur an order of magnitude earlier than QED corrections
options.C: The two correction types turn on at the same average Bjorken x
options.D: QED corrections are absent at leading residual level

questions.rationale: Their estimates for average x imply QCD corrections appear earlier, motivating use of the leading residual to illustrate interplay.
questions.evidence_quote: QCD dominant corrections happen an order of magnitude earlier than those for QED

questions.question: In the proposed pT matching procedure, what is removed from the matrix-element residuals to prevent overlap with shower evolution?

options.A: All photon radiation above the factorization scale μ
options.B: Gluon-radiation contributions at scales below μ
options.C: All virtual corrections associated with the incoming PDFs
options.D: The gluon azimuthal angle relative to the parent parton

questions.rationale: Because PDFs evolve up to μ, lower-scale gluon radiation must be omitted from residuals to avoid double counting.
questions.evidence_quote: in the residuals omit the contributions from gluon radiation at scales below μ

questions.question: How does the more accurate shower-subtracted matching proposal improve on the simple pT-veto matching?

options.A: It expands shower, exponent, and residual contributions together and matches coefficients order by order
options.B: It replaces the shower with a narrow-resonance approximation and inclusive K-factor
options.C: It averages the gluon azimuth and uses only Born-level residuals
options.D: It restricts gluon pT to values above the factorization scale to avoid PDFs

questions.rationale: The proposal derives shower-subtracted residuals by matching the combined perturbative expansion to exact results at each order.
questions.evidence_quote: required to match the respective calculated exact result for given order

questions.question: At the leading β̃0,0 level, what QED-induced change in σexp/σBorn do the authors report for LHC production?

options.A: 1.1901 with QED⊗QCD versus 1.1872 for QCD alone, about 0.3%
options.B: 1.1872 with QED⊗QCD versus 1.1901 for QCD alone, about 0.3%
options.C: 1.1911 with QED⊗QCD versus 1.1879 for QCD alone, about 3%
options.D: 1.1901 with QED⊗QCD versus 1.1879 for QCD alone, about 1.2%

questions.rationale: The LHC rows in Eq. (8) give 1.1901 and 1.1872, and the text characterizes QED as roughly 0.3%.

questions.question: What logarithm replaces the mass-regulator collinear logarithm after factorization at scale μ in the stated matching discussion?
questions.rationale: The text gives this replacement as the usual consequence of removing emissions below the factorization scale.

questions.question: Which important qualification do the authors attach to their matching schemes and claimed Monte Carlo implementation?

options.A: Both proposed shower-matching approaches are under investigation; a full MC realization is described as possible/in progress
options.B: The pT veto is proven unique and is already implemented for all mixed orders
options.C: The shower-subtracted approach is complete for heavy-boson production at all orders
options.D: Only the QED-only matching is considered, because QCD showers are unavailable

questions.rationale: They explicitly state both approaches remain under investigation and present full MC realization as a future/in-principle capability.
